reader_notes: Fluent broadsheet-columnist English; the argument arc (decline, revival, economist's caveat) is coherent end to end and the closing line "has for the moment outrun its arithmetic" is a real idiom rather than a calque.

Every gap is resolved by local collocation rather than world knowledge: withdraw services, underwrite a loss, precarious vs. the cheering headlines, ledgers looking rosy. Gap (3) is the only one that needs the wider sentence pair (expectation of half-full cabins vs. sold out), which is fair.

Minor style friction, not blocking: the long trailing absolute in "...a single bed crossing the mountains overnight sparing the traveller a wasted day at either end" makes that sentence dense on a first pass.
